newsitem.title: UK: Greene King says H2 trading started well.
newsitem.headline: Greene King says H2 trading started well.

text.p: Trading in the second half of the year has begun well, said David McCall, chairman of pub and brewing group Greene King.
The company signalled a refocused strategy which will mean investing in its retail pubs and looking for greater efficiencies in its main ale brands and brewing business.

In a statement attached to the group's half-year results, McCall announced the closure of its Biggleswade brewery and two depots as a result of the strategic review of its brewing. Management will also be restructured and non-core assets sold.
Greene King reported a 38 percent increase in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit to 15.2 million stg for the first half driven by the first contribution from the Magic Pub chain acquired in July.

"Our investment programme continues apace in both our original estate, the Magic estate and our tenancies, and we are confident that this will help to maintain the momentum in our pub business," said McCall.

Greene King said it planned to buy development sites in town centres and in out-of-town catering areas in order to improve the quality and spread of its pub estate. It will focus on three of its retailing brands -- Ale Cafe, Hungry Horse and Young People's Venues.

Greene King's brewing and wholesaling business showed a six percent dip in profits to 3.0 million stg in the 24 weeks ended October 20. Its retail pubs more than doubled profits to 13.2 million while its tenanted pubs increased profits just 0.3 million to 8.0 million.
